design: EVOLUTIONARY RULE-LIBRARY LOOP (as briefed), stated so it can be killed. Object: an archive A of interpretable position rules r: (OHLC window ≤ t, book_{t−1}) → target weights_t over the PIT 273-asset true-UTC daily panel (trader/data.py:143-190 aggregation, highs/lows/volume available — the first line in this repo that would actually read OHLC, memo §1.2 A-2). Grammar G (pre-registered, hashed): terminals = per-asset causal features {lagged returns 1/3/7/21/63d, SMA/EMA crosses, Donchian/Bollinger breakouts, Yang–Zhang/Parkinson/GK range vol, range-to-close, dollar-volume rank, cross-sectional rank/z-score, β to equal-weight market, market-VR(30) regime flag}; operators = {<,>,AND,OR,IF, sign, rank, clip, vol-scale}; sizing = {1/n equal, inverse-YZ-vol, banded target-weight with hysteresis θ·σ̂}; frequency = {H=1,2,3,5}. Search: quality-diversity (MAP-Elites) over behaviour descriptors (turnover/day, gross exposure, BEAR22 sign, long/short mix) so the archive keeps one elite per cell instead of one global winner; children by subtree crossover/mutation; population 500, ≤50 generations (Allen–Karjalainen's own budget). FITNESS (the only place the loop differs from a grid): CPCV over the PIT span 2018-10→2026-06 with N=6 contiguous groups, k=2 test groups, purge ≥ H and embargo 21d → 15 splits, 5 OOS backtest paths; per candidate the OOS-path net@21 per-decision Sharpe via the UNMODIFIED trader.backtest.cell_metrics scorer (trader/backtest.py:231-283; costs = turnover·21bp, :188-190), minus the Deflated-Sharpe rejection threshold SR₀(N_evaluated, V[SR_archive]) (Bailey–López de Prado 2014 eq.1), minus a flat-attractor penalty (gross median <0.5 or >95%-flat days ⇒ fitness −∞). MC on generated paths appears in exactly ONE role: the NULL distribution (White Reality Check / stationary bootstrap, q=0.1 as STW/B&S) and the placebo panels of the kill experiment — never as a fitness landscape. Hold-out: 2026-01→2026-06 is never touched by the loop. Output: a bill-of-materials tactic library (readable rules with turnover, exposure, per-regime net@21, DSR, trial count N) that drops straight into the tactics panel's row-1 hull/selector test (lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:103-110). PROFIT SOURCE: every rule in G is either a conditional-mean forecast (trend/reversal/breakout/cross-sectional rank), a risk premium (long β), or a cost reduction (H, hysteresis, vol-scaling); the loop itself contributes none of the three — it is a sampler over G plus an accountant of how many samples were drawn. Compute: CPU only (below). This is the honest form of the operator's 'patterns that serve Monte Carlo': the pattern library serves the MC only as the thing the MC null is computed against.
what_the_loop_learns: The learned object is (i) the archive of surviving rule trees and (ii) — the only genuinely new information — the SELECTION RECORD: N_evaluated, the empirical variance V[SR] across trials, and the behaviour-descriptor coverage. (ii) is exactly the quantity Bailey–López de Prado say every backtest must disclose and that no pre-registered grid in this repo has ever computed as a number (819 reported 'FDR 0/8' over 8 cells; 813 'BH-FDR over 132 cells'; neither computed E[max SR|null]). About the MARKET, the archive carries nothing a direct estimator would not: a rule tree is a hard-thresholded, sign-quantised forecast, so its information content is bounded above by the cross-sectional IC of its feature terminals — the exact quantity TASK_915 measures directly with Newey–West t and Bonferroni over 160 cells (tasks/TASK_915_IC_CEILING_AND_GP_BOOK.md:11-20; memo §4.2). Allen–Karjalainen (full read) found that the evolved S&P trees 'can be matched quite well with a rule that compares the normalized price to a constant … effectively similar to a 250-day moving average' and attribute the in/out asymmetry to 'low-order serial correlation in stock index returns' — GP rediscovered one lag of autocorrelation with 89 trees of 9–94 nodes. The one candidate for information beyond a linear IC is CONJUNCTIVE structure (IF vol-regime AND breakout THEN …, i.e., regime-gated or interaction terms). On this repo's surfaces that has been measured twice as ≤ linear (811: IC-max nonlinear gets 40–61% of linear; 819 CAPACITY: GBM/MLP/GRU ≈ ridge, memo §1.1 E-2), and the one structured-grammar object the program did learn — the candle-token LM with real order-dependent structure, 7.61 vs bigram 8.19 bits/tok — moved deployment alpha by +0.12pp against a +3pp bar (docs/findings/candle_language.md:86-100). Why the information would exist in daily OHLC on Kraken: only if the 915 G-A cell exists (IC ≥ 0.02, t ≥ 3, positive in 2024, 2025, 2026H1 separately). The loop cannot create it; it can at most re-express it as a threshold rule, which the fundamental law says is a WORSE harvester than the GP aim-portfolio on the same forecast (TC of a sign rule ≈ 0.5–0.7 vs the continuous controller, memo §1.3).
worth_if_ic_is_zero: Quantitatively negative, and the arithmetic is closed-form. Under H0 (every rule's true SR = 0) the archive's best in-sample Sharpe is E[max SR_N] ≈ σ_SR·[(1−γ)Z⁻¹(1−1/N) + γZ⁻¹(1−1/(Ne))], γ=0.5772 (Bailey–López de Prado 2014 eq.1, read in the primary PDF), with σ_SR ≈ 1/√T_years for an annualised Sharpe near 0. On the goalpost window 2024-01→2026-06 (T=2.5y, σ_SR=0.63): N=10 independent trials → E[max]=+1.00; N=100 → +1.60; N=1000 → +2.06. On the full PIT span 2018-10→2026-06 (7.7y, 2800 decisions, POWERED_RESULT.md:88; σ_SR=0.36): N=200 → +1.00; N=1000 → +1.17. So a null loop with as few as ~10 effectively independent trials clears the +0.97 bar in-sample on the unseen window, and ~200 do on the ENTIRE history; MinBTL (Bailey et al. 2014: 5 years supports ≤45 independent configurations at E[max SR]=1) says the same thing from the other side. The repo has already observed this law at work: 813's best-of-132 cell read fire-level Sharpe +5.81 (n=142 fires, 6 events) on a 5-month selection window and inverted to −4.08 at n=25 on the disjoint hold-out (PHASE1_MAP_PROBE.md:20, PHASE1_5_RESULT.md:6); 819's 8-cell sweep's best p≈0.01 failed BH q=0.05 (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:95). Hence: if daily IC ≈ 0, the archive is worth exactly the deflated Sharpe of its best element — DSR < 0.95 by construction — and its expected OOS Sharpe is the cost drag, ≈ −0.15 to −0.28 per regime for a 0.155/day book at 21 bp (tactics panel :62). Bailey–López de Prado add the memory-effect corollary: overfit rules that exploit mean-reverting patterns have NEGATIVE expected OOS performance, not zero. The one thing the loop is worth at IC=0 is its selection record: it produces the number N that lets the planner say how many trials the program has burned — which is diagnostic, not edge.
measured_failure_mode_and_escape: MEASURED FAILURE 1 — selection on a short window with dependent trials (813: 132 cells on a 5-month OOS window, 2 nominal GO cells, event-level n=6/28, hold-out 0/48, winner −4.08; 819: 8 cells, FDR 0/8, then PIT re-cut +0.97→+0.56 CI[−0.13,+1.23]). MECHANICAL ESCAPE: (a) N_evaluated is a pre-registered hard budget written into the SPEC hash and counted by the runner, every candidate logged — the DSR threshold SR₀(N,V) is then a number, not a hope; (b) CPCV over the full 7.7-year PIT span (15 splits, 5 OOS paths) replaces a single test window, so the selection statistic is the median OOS-path Sharpe, not one window's; (c) 2026H1 is an untouched hold-out graded once; (d) a placebo run of the identical loop on label-decoupled panels gives the EMPIRICAL null of 'best archive Sharpe', which is robust to the correlated-offspring problem that makes analytic N_eff unreliable (López de Prado 2019: N must be 'essentially independent' trials). MEASURED FAILURE 2 — the flat attractor (887: a cost-honest objective drives the policy to 91–99% HOLD and every mechanism that makes it act more loses more, monotone: −2.86%/−9.11%/−13.84% at fee 0; 892: OOS re-trims worse than a matched coin flip Δ −0.043..−0.056, every CI < 0). Under noise plus cost, the rule that trades least has the highest net Sharpe, so a GP fitness on net@21 evolves toward 'stay flat' or 'trade once'. ESCAPE: the flat penalty is a hard constraint in fitness (gross ≥ 0.5 median, no >95%-flat days, ≥1 rebalance/week), and the archive's flat share is a pre-registered FAIL band (>50% flat cells = FAIL), i.e. 887's attractor becomes a logged, gated outcome. MEASURED FAILURE 3 — instrument/epoch drift (882: two 'argmax replays' of one checkpoint disagree by Δ1.606 because the universe was resolved at different times). ESCAPE: fitness runs only through trader.backtest.cell_metrics on the pinned PIT frame from the 819 POWERED builder, epoch named per LEDGER.md:28-41. MEASURED FAILURE 4 — generated-data laundering (758 Bella-as-data 0-for-3 NULL, best +0.13pp; 804 grammar real but alpha-null). ESCAPE: generated/bootstrapped paths are used ONLY as the null (Reality Check) and the placebo, never as a fitness surface — a rule that scores on stationary-bootstrap paths with block 10 is by construction exploiting marginal/vol-clustering structure the block preserves, not conditional mean, so bootstrap fitness would select convexity/risk-premium rules and report them as edge. What the escape does NOT do: create signal. If 915 G-A fails, the loop will correctly report an empty archive after the DSR/placebo gates, which is the same information at higher cost.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: A rule library is BEAR-positive only through a rule that is short or flat in BEAR22, and the decision to be short/flat conditional on OHLC history IS a forecast (of return sign or of variance-ratio persistence). The record's only bear-positive behaviour is the trend book's short leg: BEAR22 baseline +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471 (LEDGER 898/trend-decay; tactics panel :41-43), and that leg is a sign-of-30-day-return forecast measured dead since 2024 (2024 +0.041, 2025 +0.663, 2026H1 −1.659, no CI excluding 0). The non-forecast route — a market-neutral (β-hedged) book that is bear-positive in expectation because it has no market exposure — still needs a cross-sectional forecast to have positive expectation at all (memo §1.2 A-3), and the long-only constant-mix and SPT books the panel examined are measured negative in both bears (equal-weight PIT gross −0.40 FULL / −2.54 BEAR22; tactics panel :77-81, :89-91). Bajgrowicz–Scaillet (full read, p.24-25) add the cost side: their FDR-selected rule portfolios were short >20% of days and lending fees of 5–20 bp/yr alone erased early-period OOS performance; on Kraken spot a short leg is not even available without perps (898 long-flat variant 2026H1 −5.221). Conditional clause: an evolved library can be MADE bear-positive by construction (a flat or β-hedged cell in the MAP-Elites archive), but then it is bear-zero, not bear-positive, and the goalpost is +0.97 net, not 0.

literature.ref: Allen & Karjalainen 1999, 'Using genetic algorithms to find technical trading rules', JFE 51:245-271
literature.claim: GP over an MA/max/min/logic grammar on S&P 500 1928-1995 finds rules with no consistent OOS excess return after costs; rules reduce to low-order serial-correlation timing.
literature.numbers: Population 500, ≤50 generations, 10 training periods × 10 trials = 100 trials, 89 rules saved; one-way cost 0.25%: average OOS excess return −2.05%/yr (negative in 9/10 test periods), 3.8 trades/yr, long 57% of days; at 0.1% cost −1.02%/yr (6/10 negative, 18 trades/yr); at 0.5% −2.36%/yr (9/10 negative, 1.4 trades/yr). In-vs-out daily return difference significant for 36/89 rules; rule volatility 10.0% vs index 14.7%. Rules 'effectively similar to a 250-day moving average'.

literature.ref: Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999, 'Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap', JF 54(5):1647-1691 (LSE FMG DP303 read)
literature.claim: White's Reality Check over the full rule universe: BLL's 100-year DJIA result survives snooping, but the 10-year OOS period and the S&P 500 futures show no rule outperforms once the universe is accounted for.
literature.numbers: 7,846 rules (497 filter, 2,049 MA, 1,220 S&R, 2,040 channel, 2,040 OBV). Full DJIA 1897-1996 best rule 17.17%/yr, 6,310 trades (63.1/yr), break-even cost 0.27%/trade, RC p<0.002; B&H Sharpe 0.034 vs best-rule Sharpe 0.82. OOS DJIA 1987-1996: the 1986-selected 5-day MA earned 2.8%/yr, nominal p 0.322; BLL-universe best 8.5%/yr, RC p 0.15 vs nominal 0.05; Sharpe criterion RC p 0.72 vs nominal 0.12. S&P 500 futures 1984-1996 full universe: best ≈10%/yr, nominal p 0.04, RC p 0.90; Sharpe criterion RC p 0.99 vs nominal <0.002. Bonferroni over 8,000 rules gives 'p<1' where RC gives 0.05 — RC is the right correction for dependent rules.

literature.ref: Bajgrowicz & Scaillet 2012, 'Technical trading revisited: False discoveries, persistence tests, and transaction costs', JFE 106(3):473-491 (UNIGE accepted manuscript read: abstract, intro, §5 persistence, §6, appendices)
literature.claim: FDR⁺ rule selection is far more powerful than Reality Check/Romano-Wolf, yet ex-ante-selected rule portfolios (monthly re-selection) have no persistent OOS performance and low costs erase what remains.
literature.numbers: Same 7,846 rules, DJIA 1897-2011. MC (Sharpe pair 3/−3): 10%-FDR⁺ portfolio detects 52.6% of true outperformers at achieved FDR 9.7%; 5%-RW detects 0.6%, 20%-RW 4.7%; median rank of the first lucky rule 422nd. Persistence: OOS performance 'negative in most cases throughout the recent periods'; <5% of rules remain in the portfolio after one rebalancing; one-way costs of <5 to 35 bp offset any OOS performance even in early periods; FDR⁺ portfolio short >20% of days, lending fees 5-20 bp/yr suffice to kill 1897-1962; 'in recent periods … we do not detect genuine performance already before transaction costs'.

literature.ref: Bailey & López de Prado 2014, 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio', J. Portfolio Management (SSRN 2460551; read)
literature.claim: Expected maximum Sharpe of N null trials and the DSR test that deflates a selected Sharpe for trials, variance across trials, sample length, skew and kurtosis.
literature.numbers: E[max SR_N] ≈ E[SR] + √V[SR]·((1−γ)Z⁻¹[1−1/N] + γZ⁻¹[1−1/(Ne)]), γ≈0.5772 (eq.1). DSR = Z[(SR−SR₀)√(T−1)/√(1−γ₃SR+((γ₄−1)/4)SR²)] (eq.2). Example: N=100, V[SR]=1/2, T=1250 daily, skew −3, kurt 10, SR 2.5 annualised → SR₀=0.1132 (daily units), DSR=0.9004<0.95 → reject; with N=46 DSR=0.9505; with normal returns N=88 needed. Holdout 'cannot prevent backtest overfitting'.

literature.ref: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu 2014/2015, 'Pseudo-mathematics and financial charlatanism' (Notices AMS) / 'The Probability of Backtest Overfitting' (J. Comp. Finance)
literature.claim: Minimum backtest length grows with ln N of independent configurations; CSCV/PBO estimates the probability that the IS-optimal strategy underperforms the OOS median.
literature.numbers: MinBTL < 2·ln N / E[max SR]² years (upper bound); with 5 years of data no more than ≈45 independent configurations at E[max SR]=1 before the expected OOS Sharpe of the selected strategy is 0. Applied to this repo: 2.5-year window → N≈10; 7.7-year PIT span → N≈200 (computed with eq.1 above, σ_SR=1/√T).

literature.ref: Harvey, Liu & Zhu 2016, '… and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', RFS 29(1):5-68; Harvey & Liu 2015, 'Backtesting', JPM 42(1)
literature.claim: Multiple-testing hurdle for a new predictor is t>3.0; Sharpe haircuts under multiple testing are nonlinear (marginal Sharpes heavily penalised).
literature.numbers: 316 published factors; t-hurdle 3.0 (vs 1.96). The repo's TASK_915 gate (NW t ≥ 3 after Bonferroni over 160 cells) is this hurdle.

literature.ref: Hsu & Kuan 2005, 'Reexamining the Profitability of Technical Analysis with Data Snooping Checks', J. Financial Econometrics 3(4):606-628
literature.claim: With Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over simple rules plus complex strategies, significant rules exist for NASDAQ Composite and Russell 2000 (young markets) but not DJIA/S&P 500.
literature.numbers: 4 indices; RC + SPA; positive only for the two 'newer-company' indices — the usual argument for crypto being young enough; the repo's 898 decay 2021→2026 is the counter-observation on this venue.

literature.ref: Neely, Weller & Dittmar 1997 (JFQA); Neely & Weller 2003, 'Intraday technical trading in the foreign exchange market', JIMF 22:223-237; Neely, Weller & Ulrich 2009, 'The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis', JFQA 44(2)
literature.claim: GP-evolved FX rules had genuine 1981-1995 OOS excess returns at daily frequency; at intraday frequency with realistic costs and hours there is no evidence of excess returns; the daily-rule profits had disappeared by the early 1990s.
literature.numbers: 1981-95 OOS excess returns roughly 1-7%/yr (daily, 6 currencies); intraday GP vs optimised linear model: 'no evidence of excess returns' after realistic costs on DEM/JPY/GBP/CHF; filter and MA profits gone by early 1990s.

literature.ref: Fang, Jacobsen & Qin 2014, 'Predictability of the simple technical trading rules: An out-of-sample test', Review of Financial Economics 23(1):30-45
literature.claim: The exact BLL 1992 rules show no predictability 1987-2011; the authors attribute the earlier success to bias rather than to markets becoming efficient.
literature.numbers: True OOS 1987-2011, same 26 rules; no evidence of predictive power.

literature.ref: Anghel 2021, 'A reality check on trading rule performance in the cryptocurrency market: Machine learning vs. technical analysis', Finance Research Letters 39
literature.claim: Reality-Check-corrected ML and TA rules rarely deliver statistically significant positive excess returns in crypto; ML beats TA only on small illiquid coins.
literature.numbers: 'Statistically significant positive excess returns are rarely achieved'; advantage concentrated in small/illiquid cryptocurrencies.

literature.ref: Hudson & Urquhart 2021, 'Technical trading and cryptocurrencies', Annals of Operations Research 297:191-220
literature.claim: The pro-TA crypto result: ~15,000 rules over 5 crypto markets show significant predictability surviving several multiple-hypothesis procedures, with breakeven costs above typical crypto costs — but Bitcoin shows NO out-of-sample predictability.
literature.numbers: ≈15,000 rules, 2 BTC markets + 3 other coins, pre-2019 sample; 'breakeven transaction costs substantially higher than those typically found'; Bitcoin: no OOS predictability, other coins: yes. The sample predates the 2024-2026 window where 898 measures the repo's own trend rule dead.

literature.ref: López de Prado 2014, 'Determining Optimal Trading Rules without Backtesting', arXiv:1408.1159
literature.claim: Profit-taking/stop-loss rules can be derived on synthetic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths without a historical backtest, but the answer is entirely a function of the fitted OU parameters — the generator's assumed mean reversion is what the rule harvests.
literature.numbers: Discrete OU; 'we conjecture its existence on the basis of the empirical evidence presented' — no closed form; result inherits the generator.

literature.ref: Sun et al. 2022, 'Backtesting Trading Strategies with GAN To Avoid Overfitting', arXiv:2209.04895 (2018 thesis, translated)
literature.claim: Proposes validating strategies on GAN-LSTM paths fit to historical distribution; the available text gives no quantitative evidence that this reduces OOS overfitting versus historical validation.
literature.numbers: No numbers in the abstract; authors flag statements as 'outdated in 2022'.

literature.ref: Cont, Cucuringu, Xu & Zhang, 'Tail-GAN: Learning to Simulate Tail Risk Scenarios', Management Science 72(4):2917-2936 (2026; arXiv 2203.01664)
literature.claim: A generator is only faithful for the strategies whose P&L functionals it was trained to match (VaR/ES of a strategy set); generic fidelity does not transfer to arbitrary rule P&L — the formal version of 'generated-path fitness launders the generator'.
literature.numbers: Loss built on joint elicitability of VaR and ES of a fixed strategy class; generalises to that class.

literature.ref: 'Diverse Approaches to Optimal Execution Schedule Generation', arXiv:2601.22113 (MAP-Elites for trade execution)
literature.claim: Only published MAP-Elites trading application found: modest QD runs failed to generalise; the large run improves niche specialists while other cells degrade.
literature.numbers: 500 iterations × 256 children = 128,000 candidate policies, 5.5 h on an M4 Max (CPU); 30-100 iteration configs 'failed to generalise'; specialists +8-10% within their niche, degradation elsewhere.

literature.ref: Alpha-GPT (Wang et al. 2023, arXiv:2308.00016); AlphaAgent (2025, arXiv:2502.16789); AlphaForge, AlphaGen (formulaic alpha mining, GP/RL/LLM)
literature.claim: The modern GP/LLM 'alpha factory' literature reports IC-scale results on thousands-of-stocks A-share panels and itself names GP-mined alphas as prone to rapid decay from overfitting.
literature.numbers: Alpha-GPT average top-20 OOS IC 0.0095-0.0115 before vs 0.0216-0.0276 after search enhancement (breadth ≈3,000+ stocks, where IC 0.02 is tradable; on a 273-asset panel with N_eff 5-15 it is not, memo §1.3); AlphaAgent: 'traditional methods such as genetic programming prone to rapid alpha decay'.

literature.ref: López de Prado 2019, 'A Data Science Solution to the Multiple-Testing Crisis in Financial Research', J. Financial Data Science 1(1):99-110
literature.claim: Selection bias reduces to (a) the number of essentially independent trials and (b) the variance across trials; correlated trials (GP offspring, neighbouring grid cells) must be clustered before N enters the DSR.
literature.numbers: Worked DSR example on a real strategy family; N from clustering of trial return correlations.

honest_use: Bounded to three roles, none of which is 'source of edge'. (1) TRIAL ACCOUNTANT for the tactic library (tactics panel row 1): a small, hashed grammar (target N_eff ≤ 200 for the full PIT span, ≤ 50 for anything graded on 2024-26 alone, per the E[max] arithmetic) whose runner logs every evaluation and reports DSR with N = total evaluated, so the program's next 'best cell' comes with the number that says how many draws produced it. This is the one thing a pre-registered grid does not currently emit. (2) NULL CALIBRATOR: run the same rule family on label-decoupled panels (positions on real features, returns circularly shifted by a common offset ≥365 d so cross-sectional structure and vol clustering survive but conditional mean dies) to obtain the empirical distribution of 'best-of-archive Sharpe' — White's Reality Check with the repo's own scorer. This calibrates 813-style GO cells before any Phase-2 build and is reusable by TASK_915 as a second read on its Bonferroni. (3) CONVERTER, conditional on 915 G-A PASS: if a feature family carries IC, the QD archive can express it as a readable, turnover-bounded rule for the operator's 'hold on policy' requirement — but the Gârleanu–Pedersen book on the same forecast is the higher-TC harvester, so the rule is a deployability/auditability concession costing ~30-50% of gross IR (TC 0.5-0.7 for sign rules), not an improvement. Not a legitimate use: as a fitness landscape on Bella/bootstrap paths (selects generator structure), as an unbounded open-ended search (N grows without the bar moving), as a MuZero 'policy = rule library' loop (the K-arm selector's timing term is a forecast over ~30 monthly decisions with SE ≈ 0.18 σ_month, tactics panel :47-54). Verdict on the row question: NOT worth a separate row. Fold the trial counter + DSR + placebo into row 1 of the tactics panel and into TASK_915's SPEC as a reporting requirement; run TASK_915 first because its FAIL branch empties every rule archive in advance.
compute: CPU only; the 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to this design. Unit cost from the record: one full config through trader.backtest.cell_metrics with 2000-draw block-bootstrap CIs on the 2800×273 PIT daily panel = 82.2 s single-core (POWERED_RESULT.md:100); without the bootstrap a rule evaluation is a vectorised numpy pass over a 2800×273 array (≈6 MB) ≈ 0.5-2 s; 813's 132-cell map on MINUTE data ran 1282 s at 1.98 GB RSS (PHASE1_MAP_PROBE.md:10). Budgeted run: population 500 × 50 generations = 25,000 evaluations × CPCV (rules have no fitted parameters, so the 15 splits are a partition of one evaluation, cost ≈1.2×) ≈ 25,000 × 1.5 s ≈ 10 CPU-hours single-core → ~20 min on 32 cores; bootstrap CIs only for the ≤50 archive elites ≈ 70 CPU-min; 20 placebo panels × the same loop ≈ 200 CPU-hours → ~6 h on 32 cores. Total ≤ 1 CPU-day wall on gpu-server CPU under safe_run (or overnight on the workstation's CPU under the allocation contract), zero GPU-hours, RAM < 4 GB. Build: ~2 days (grammar + evaluator ≈ 400 lines, MAP-Elites loop ≈ 150, CPCV/DSR/placebo harness ≈ 200, all importing trader/backtest.py and the 819 POWERED PIT builder). If MC fitness on generated paths were adopted instead (it should not be), Bella generation of K futures per state would move this to GPU-days — the single case where the 64 GB cards would matter, and it is the case the design rejects.

kill_experiment.design: One pre-registered run, SPEC hashed before launch (grammar G, N_budget = 25,000 evaluations, CPCV N=6/k=2 purge≥H embargo 21d, activity floor, bands). Arm R (real): the loop on the PIT 273-asset true-daily OHLC panel 2018-10→2025-12, hold-out 2026-01→2026-06 never read by the loop. Arm P (placebo, 20 seeds): the identical loop, identical budget, on panels where positions are computed from the real feature panel but applied to a return panel circularly shifted by one common random offset ≥ 365 d (kills conditional mean; keeps marginals, vol clustering, cross-sectional co-movement, and the flat attractor). Arm B (bootstrap null): for the real archive's best 10 elites, White Reality Check p-values via stationary bootstrap with block length from the 901 certified range estimator, B=1000. Statistics recorded for every arm: best archive element's median CPCV-OOS-path net@21, its 2026H1 hold-out net@21, DSR with N=25,000 and V[SR] from the archive, flat share of the archive, gross median, BEAR22 sign.
kill_experiment.instrument: Unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics (seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21, trader/backtest.py:231) on the 819 POWERED point-in-time builder's frame, pinned and epoch-named per LEDGER.md:28-41 (post-E-d, daily table current to the 899 seam). DSR computed from Bailey–López de Prado eq.1-2 with skew/kurtosis of the elite's net series. Optional second instrument for any elite that passes: eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax with the rule's weights quantised to the ±w_unit ladder, agreement within 0.1 (the 882 discipline).
kill_experiment.pass_fail: PASS (the loop is not a noise amplifier on this surface) requires ALL of: (i) real best-elite hold-out 2026H1 net@21 ≥ +0.97 AND median CPCV-OOS-path net@21 ≥ +0.97 with block-bootstrap CI lo > 0; (ii) real best-elite statistic > the 95th percentile of the 20 placebo best-elite statistics (both hold-out and CPCV-path); (iii) DSR ≥ 0.95 at N=25,000; (iv) Reality Check p < 0.05 for that elite within the archive universe; (v) archive flat share < 50%, elite gross median ≥ 0.5, BEAR22 net@21 > 0 (in-sample form check). MARGINAL: (i) at ≥ +0.56 with (ii)-(v) holding → record as a PIT-bar tactic, not a goalpost pass. FAIL: any of (ii)-(iv) fails, or the real archive is statistically indistinguishable from the placebo archives (real best within the placebo IQR) → the evolutionary family is retired for daily OHLC on this venue; the recorded N and placebo distribution become the standing multiplicity reference for every later rule grid. Pre-committed reading if 915 G-A has already FAILED when this runs: do not run; the archive is empty by construction.
kill_experiment.cost: ≈2 days build reusing trader/backtest.py, the 819 PIT builder and 901's range estimator; ≤1 CPU-day wall (≈250 CPU-hours total, dominated by the 20 placebo loops); zero GPU; RAM < 4 GB; kill date 10 days from SPEC commit. Runs on gpu-server CPU under safe_run per .claude/rules/10-compute-allocation.md (pure reads of the DB, no writes).

honest_odds: P(the evolutionary loop, run honestly as above, yields an elite clearing +0.97 net@21 PIT on 2024-01→2026-06 with DSR ≥ 0.95 and placebo-beating) ≈ 2-4% — the same band the tactics panel put on its whole family (3-5%), because the loop shares every term of the fundamental law with the direct estimator and adds a multiplicity tax. P(it finds an OOS-verified edge that TASK_915's cross-sectional IC sweep would NOT find) < 1%: that would require a conjunctive/regime-gated structure with zero linear IC in every feature family at every horizon, against 811/819-CAPACITY's nonlinear ≤ linear reads and Allen–Karjalainen's finding that evolved trees reduce to low-order autocorrelation. Conditional on 915 G-A PASS, P(the archive contains a readable rule at ≥ +0.56 PIT) ≈ 25-35%, but the Gârleanu–Pedersen book on the same cell dominates it on TC, so the loop's marginal value even then is auditability, not Sharpe. P(a loop run WITHOUT the DSR/placebo gates reports a bar-clearing rule) ≈ 1 by the E[max] arithmetic (N ≥ 10 on the 2.5-year window suffices), which is the operator's 'faint hope' made precise: the hope is real and it is the hope of finding the maximum of noise. Stated prior on the load-bearing doubt, unchanged from the memo: P(daily OHLC, PIT, clears +0.56 under honest costs) ≈ 25%, +0.97 ≈ 10-15%; the loop does not move it.
open_doubts: Conjunctive/regime-gated rules are the one structure a linear IC cannot see. The two nonlinear≤linear reads (811 on minute data; 819 CAPACITY on a pooled, non-demeaned 20-asset target) are weak instruments for that claim on the PIT daily panel (memo §1.1 E-2). The tactics panel's VR-persistence gate row is the cheaper direct test of the only gated family with a mechanism; if it shows VR persistence, a small gated grammar becomes worth a hashed N ≤ 50 run.

Hudson & Urquhart 2021 report MHT-corrected TA profitability on altcoins (not BTC) with breakeven costs above typical — the strongest published counter-evidence to 'rules are dead in crypto'. Its sample predates 2019 and the repo measures its own trend rule dead 2024-2026 (898); whether alt-specific rules survive on Kraken's PIT panel post-2024 is unmeasured and is exactly what a small pre-registered grid, not an open GP, should check.

N_eff for a GP population is ill-defined: offspring are correlated and MAP-Elites niches share ancestry. The analytic DSR is sensitive to N (paper: N=46 vs 100 flips the verdict); the placebo distribution is the robust substitute but costs 20× the compute and its difficulty must match reality — a per-asset circular shift destroys cross-asset alignment and lowers book vol, biasing the placebo weak; the design uses a common offset for that reason, and this choice should be checked by comparing placebo-book vol to real-book vol.

Bailey–López de Prado's holdout warning applies to the 2026H1 hold-out: 6 months of daily decisions (σ_SR ≈ 1.4) cannot separate +0.97 from 0 on its own; the hold-out is a sign/consistency check, the CPCV paths and the placebo carry the verdict. 875 measured OOS seed spread 1.0-2.0 on half-year windows for the same reason.

The flat-attractor penalty is a design choice that can itself be gamed: a rule that holds a constant 1/n long book satisfies gross ≥ 0.5 and is a β bet (equal-weight PIT gross −0.40 FULL / −2.54 BEAR22). The BEAR22 form check catches this in-sample only; the panel's β-hedged constant-mix cell is the right control arm.

Execution variants (H=3, hysteresis, hold-shares accounting) belong to the tactics panel's row 2 as cost reduction (+0.10..+0.15 expected). If they are in the grammar, the loop will find them and the archive will report cost savings as edge; either exclude them from G or attribute them separately in the report.

Whether a readable rule is more deployable than a checkpoint is asserted, not measured: 898 shows readability did not prevent the trend rule's decay, and Bajgrowicz–Scaillet show <5% of FDR-selected rules survive one monthly re-selection. 'Hold on policy' buys auditability, not stability.

This consultation read Bajgrowicz–Scaillet's tables only through the text (Tables 4-6 not seen) and Hudson–Urquhart at abstract level; the STW and Allen–Karjalainen numbers are from the primary PDFs. No repo code was run; all repo numbers are re-read from result files and the LEDGER.
